detail: Following her election as Mayor of Strasbourg in March 2026, Catherine Trautmann was elected President of the Eurométropole de Strasbourg on 10 April 2026 (80 of 107 votes), surrounding herself with 18 vice-presidents. The Eurométropole is a public intercommunal authority (établissement public de coopération intercommunale), not a commercial company; the presidency carries no ownership stake. She retained the transport portfolio for herself. She had previously been President of the Communauté urbaine de Strasbourg / Eurométropole during earlier mandates.

Mayor of Strasbourg. Re-elected in the March 2026 municipal elections (37% at the second round, ahead of Jeanne Barseghian and Jean-Philippe Vetter), returning to the Hôtel de Ville some 25 years after her previous mandate. The mayoralty is an elected public office, not a corporate role; it confers ex-officio representation in numerous local public companies (SEM/SPL such as CTS, Parcus, Habitation Moderne, Locusem, SPL Deux-Rives) via designation by the council.

ownership_stake: n/a (public establishment; State and Ville de Strasbourg joint governance)
detail: President of the Board of Directors (conseil d'administration) of the Port autonome de Strasbourg, a public port establishment jointly governed by the French State and the Ville de Strasbourg. She was renewed as a board member by a Strasbourg city council decision of 28 December 2014. She was succeeded by Anne-Marie Jean, elected president by the board on 8 October 2020.

entity: European Commission – TEN-T North Sea–Baltic core network corridor
detail: European Coordinator for the trans-European transport (TEN-T) North Sea–Baltic core network corridor, appointed by the European Commission. This is an EU institutional/advisory mandate (a 2,500 km multimodal corridor linking Helsinki/Tallinn to North Sea ports), not a corporate directorship; mandate terms run four years and are renewable. She has continued to be cited in this role through 2024–2026.
